title: Fixed on with singular owners
summary: Use fixed on with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä to say what the owner has.
objectives: Use fixed on with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä to say what the owner has.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Use fixed on with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä to say what the owner has.
Minulla on pallo means “I have a ball”. The owner phrase takes on; an “I am” statement would use olen.
keyPoints: Use fixed on with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä to say what the owner has.

steps: Use fixed on for possession with minulla; olen belongs to an “I am” sentence.
kirja (“book”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Sinulla still takes on, not olet: this pattern says what someone has.
koira (“dog”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Hänellä on means “she has” or “he has”; the gender choice does not change on.
auto (“car”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Changing the thing to a cat leaves the same sinulla on pattern.
kissa (“cat”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.

commonMistakes: Keep on with minulla, sinulla and hänellä; do not replace it with a subject-agreeing verb.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses fixed on with minulla, sinulla and hänellä.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed on in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: In “Sinulla on tyyny.” (“You have a pillow.”), which word means “have”? Address one person. Write only that word.
practiceExercises.explanation: On expresses possession. Sinulla identifies the owner, and tyyny names the pillow.
